Visit note | 2025-11-10 10:30 AM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Hafsa Hasan, 35, female. Mrs. Hasan explains that she has been experiencing a terrifying fear of dying during sudden episodes, even though her heart checks have always come back normal. Her anchor vital shows about 11 panic attacks in the last month. She works as a ride-share driver, and her anchor context reveals that her very first attack happened in a crowded lift in Gazipur. She has a known comorbidity of Bronchial asthma. On examination, other vitals are: BP 110/79 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 47 kg. Mental state examination shows normal cognition and tense affect without signs of psychosis. Assessment: Panic disorder. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice given to the patient: practise slow breathing during attacks; reduce caffeine; start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.
